.pmx dt { color: var(--muted); }
.pmx dd { margin: 0; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.pmx .chart { width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }

.pmx .legend { display: flex; gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--muted); margin-top: 0.25rem; }

.pmx ol.steps {
  list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0 0 2.25rem;

}
.pmx .steps li {
  counter-increment: step; position: relative;

.pmx .files a, .pmx code.f { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.85rem; }

.pmx .btn {

## What you report

Five answers, each defined in section 9 of `sap.md`. Report only what your analysis supports.

| Key | What it asks |
|---|---|
| `structural_ncmt` | How many compartments the final model has |
| `disposition_params` | Typical CL, volumes and distribution parameters at 70 kg |
| `error_model` | The residual error terms |
| `cov_effects` | Which covariates act on which parameter, and how strongly |
| `outlier_records` | The `ROWID`s of any records you flagged as data errors |

## How it works

Every scenario is simulated from a known model, so there is a right answer, and a few realistic
problems are planted in the data on purpose. Scenario 00 is open: its answer key and the script
that built it are public in
[`template_scenario_00`](https://github.com/AIML-SIG/Agentic-workflows/tree/main/tools/pmxbench/template_scenario_00),
which shows how every scenario is put together. From scenario 01 on, only the data, the SAP and
the template are published; the answer key stays private, so scores can't be looked up.

Scores and past runs are on the [leaderboard](leaderboard.qmd). The files live in
[`tools/pmxbench`](https://github.com/AIML-SIG/Agentic-workflows/tree/main/tools/pmxbench).
